questions.q: What does OpenID Connect (OIDC) add on top of OAuth 2.0?
o: An identity layer that tells the client who the user is
A faster way of refreshing access tokens
Encryption for every API response
A new transport protocol for tokens
questions.w: OAuth 2.0 answers what the app may access. OIDC answers who logged in, using an ID token and the userinfo endpoint.

questions.q: Which token carries the user's identity claims for the client app?
o: The ID token
The access token
The refresh token
The authorization code
questions.w: The ID token is a JWT meant for the client. The access token is meant for the API and should not be parsed by the client for identity.

questions.q: Which scope tells the server you want an OIDC login rather than plain OAuth?
o: `openid`
`profile`
`offline_access`
`login`
questions.w: Without `openid` the response is plain OAuth 2.0. `profile` and `email` request extra claims. `offline_access` requests a refresh token.

questions.q: What is the `nonce` in an OIDC request for?
o: It ties the ID token to the request, so a captured token can't be replayed
It sets how long the user's session stays valid at the provider
It encrypts the ID token so only the client can read it
It picks which signature algorithm the provider will use
questions.w: The client sends a random value and checks that the same value appears inside the ID token.

questions.q: What must a client check in an ID token before trusting it?
o: Signature, issuer, audience (its own client id), expiry and nonce
Only that the string is a validly formed JWT token
Only that the same token has not been seen earlier today
Only that the user name inside the token is not empty
questions.w: The `aud` must match the client, otherwise a token issued for another app could be replayed against yours.

questions.q: How does a client discover the endpoints and signing keys of an OIDC provider?
o: From the discovery document at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`
By hard-coding the values after reading them in a blog post
By scanning the open ports of the provider's servers
By asking each user to paste the endpoints in manually
questions.w: The discovery document lists the issuer, authorization and token endpoints and `jwks_uri`, where the public keys rotate.

questions.q: A resource server receives an ID token in the `Authorization` header instead of an access token. What is the right response?
o: Reject it, since ID tokens are for the client, not for APIs
Accept it, because it holds the user's name
Accept it only for read requests
Convert it into an access token first
questions.w: Mixing up the two tokens is a common mistake. APIs should validate access tokens with the correct audience.

questions.q: What does single sign-on (SSO) give users through OIDC?
o: One login at an identity provider that many apps trust
One password reused across all the apps
One shared cookie across every domain
One token that never expires
questions.w: Apps redirect to the identity provider. If the user already has a session there, they get back a token without typing credentials again.
